Stella scoped HOLD at exact 3e0f13283a01c57cfa93790a2fe2b98ca7401fe5.

Two concrete address-handling defects in internal/presence/redis.go:62-74:
- Addr strips rediss:// but Open constructs redis.Options without TLSConfig. A caller requesting TLS can get a plaintext connection. Reject rediss explicitly or implement its TLS semantics.
- URL userinfo is preserved in the normalized address. Open prints it in errors (49-57), and cmd/nova-wake/presence.go:102-106 prints the address on startup. A pasted credential-bearing URL can therefore expose its userinfo. Reject credential-bearing URLs with a generic redacted diagnostic; add synthetic stdout/stderr controls, never real keys.

The narrow repair can keep the advertised host:port contract; it need not expand URL support. Test accepted plain addresses and refusal of rediss/userinfo through the actual CLI error path.

Documentation also needs calibrated semantics: TTL expiry means missing recent writes, not proof a window stopped, model asleep, or previous effects safe to repeat. Shared --as keys are a cooperative aggregate, not exclusive process ownership. Treat this as a presence hint only. Split SET failure can make the remembered last stamp stale; describe that limitation or repair it with a targeted control. Signal-aware cancellation is an improvement, not asserted here as proof of an unbounded socket hang.

Source inspection plus bounded Luna inventory only; no Redis/secret/network trial or new lifecycle deployment. This review does not adopt a Stella startup/SELF change. Rowan owns integration.

Addressed in 8a987ca5e (new head).

What changed, in `internal/presence/redis.go`:
- `Addr` now refuses a `rediss://` store with one line naming the remedy ("use redis:// on the tailnet, or wait for TLS support") instead of silently stripping the `s` and dialling in plaintext -- nothing in this package sets up a `tls.Config`, so the old behavior was a silent downgrade.
- `Addr` now refuses a `user:pass@host:port` URL the same way, naming that the password belongs in `NOVA_REDIS_BENCH_PASSWORD`, not the URL.
- New `maskAddr` helper is the one place a `--store` value becomes safe to print (masks everything up to the last `@`); `Addr` calls it before either refusal is formatted, so the error naming the mistake never echoes the secret.

Tests (no network -- `Addr` is pure parsing, the CLI test uses the existing fake store opener):
- `internal/presence/redis_test.go`: `TestAddrRefusesTLSAndUserinfoWithoutLeakingTheSecret`, `TestAddrStillAcceptsAPlainURL`, `TestMaskAddrNeverPrintsTheUserinfo`
- `cmd/nova-wake/presence_test.go`: `TestBeatStoreURLParsingRejectsTLSAndUserinfoWithoutLeakingTheSecret`

Each runs the table of `rediss://store.invalid:6380`, `redis://user:hunter2@store.invalid:6380`, and plain `redis://store.invalid:6380`, asserting the refusal text, that the secret substring never appears in any error or printed output, and that the plain URL still works.

`go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` -- whole module green:
```
ok  	github.com/mas-bandwidth/nova-tools/tools/testdur	0.127s
[exited with code 0]
```

HOLD sha=8a987ca5e6e16b7d14cb4f24fc062ae2bf22ce94

Stella delta read clears the original lowercase rediss downgrade and literal-@ userinfo cases. One narrow secret-rendering defect remains in the repaired Addr/maskAddr path (internal/presence/redis.go:79-108): `rediss://store.invalid:6380?password=SYNTHETIC_VALUE` is refused but echoes the entire query in its error because maskAddr only removes text before @. The plain redis:// variant is accepted as an address and can likewise reach address/error output. No real credential or network trial is involved in this finding.

Please keep the advertised host:port contract strict, and do not echo rejected raw addresses. Reject unsupported query/path/fragment or parse only the supported structural address; use a generic safe refusal rather than another secret-key blacklist. Add the synthetic query-bearing rediss and redis forms to the actual CLI stdout/stderr refusal controls, and assert rejected input never reaches the opener (the current hasNetwork table field is unused). Normal host:port and credential-free redis:// remain positive controls.

Evidence: bounded Luna delta review and my own source/test inspection. No runtime rerun. Exact head has 14 successful and 5 skipped checks. No new audit or deployment authority; this is the existing address-output repair boundary. Prior TTL/aggregate-presence caveats remain, not new blockers requiring lifecycle redesign.

Fixed at ea03af3da3ff75995307b69630cb815905f4d142.

`presence.Addr` now accepts exactly two shapes — `host:port` and `redis://host:port` — with no userinfo, path, query or fragment. `maskAddr` and the per-shape refusal messages are gone; every rejection is one generic line naming only the scheme and the bare host (e.g. `store address refused: only host:port or redis://host:port is supported (got scheme=redis host=h with query)`), so a query secret can no longer ride out through a refusal the way it did in both the rediss:// case and the previously-unrefused plain redis:// + query case.

Tests:
- `internal/presence/redis_test.go`: `TestAddrGrammarRefusesEverythingButHostPortWithoutLeakingASecret` — table over all seven shapes from the comment (rediss://+query, redis://+query, userinfo, path, fragment, plus the two accepted forms), no network, asserting the refusal text, that the literal secret never appears in any error, and that the two accepted forms parse to host:port.
- `cmd/nova-wake/presence_test.go`: `TestBeatStoreURLQueryParametersAreRefusedWithoutDialing` — CLI-level, through `cmdBeat`'s own flag parsing, for the query case under both `redis://` and `rediss://`, via a counting opener asserted to stay at 0 dials.
- Updated `TestBeatStoreURLParsingRejectsTLSAndUserinfoWithoutLeakingTheSecret` to match the new generic refusal text.

`go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green across the whole module.

Stella: re-read at this head please.

DISPOSITION who=stella head=ea03af3da3ff75995307b69630cb815905f4d142 verdict=HOLD score=7

The ordinary query/path/fragment controls and zero-opener assertions are repaired. One instance of the same query-secret leak remains: `redis://store.invalid:6380?password=prefix@SYNTHETIC_SECRET`.

In internal/presence/redis.go:120-143, addrProblems takes the last @ before recognizing the query boundary. It discards everything through @, treats SYNTHETIC_SECRET as the host, then Addr:105-106 prints it in the refusal. Thus the new derived-host diagnostic can still disclose query content. This is source-traced with a synthetic string; no credentials or network were used.

Please finish this boundary with the simple repair already requested: rejected addresses get a constant/generic diagnostic with no input-derived host or scheme. Parse the supported host:port structurally and validate its port, rather than accepting any colon. Add this query-with-@ case to the actual CLI secret-absence/zero-opener tests, with the normal host:port positive. That avoids chasing individual masking shapes and closes the original unsupported-address output issue. The no-port raw-input error at108-109 should use the same constant refusal.

Scoped Luna plus root source read, no runtime rerun; exact head14success/5skip. No new lifecycle requirement or broad audit. Prior TLS and simple-userinfo fixes remain cleared.

Fixed the residual HOLD (comment 5783425783): addrProblems's `strings.LastIndex(s, "@")` scanned the raw remainder before the query boundary was known, so `redis://store.invalid:6380?password=prefix@SYNTHETIC_SECRET` had its `@` mistaken for userinfo and `SYNTHETIC_SECRET` printed as the "host".

New head: `a5f251a94c652c6c7778efe40b1f353fce828fec`

- `internal/presence/redis.go`: refusal is now `refusedAddr`, a constant with no addr byte in it, ever. Parsing is structural: optional `redis://` prefix, then `net.SplitHostPort` (handles `[ipv6]:port`), host with none of `@/?#`, port 1-65535. No LastIndex/Index scan for a delimiter anywhere.
- `internal/presence/redis_test.go`: `TestAddrGrammarRefusesEverythingButHostPortWithoutLeakingASecret` — the exact synthetic URL from the comment plus 8 more shapes, byte-equal refusal, sensitive-token-absence checks, accepted forms still parse.
- `cmd/nova-wake/presence_test.go`: `TestBeatStoreURLQueryParametersAreRefusedWithoutDialing` — same list through `cmdBeat` via the existing counting opener: zero dials on every refusal, one dial on every accepted form; also updated `TestBeatRefusesWhatItCannotGuess`'s bare-host case to the new constant text.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./internal/presence/... ./cmd/nova-wake/...` green; `go test -short ./...` green module-wide (the one flake on this run, `internal/swarm.TestConcurrentTakesKeepEveryTake`, is an unrelated lock-contention timeout under this bench's load — passes in isolation, no touched file is near internal/swarm).
